accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Finite tail selection, positive basin mass, and the common Cesaro attraction modulus are assumed class restrictions, not established for the Guo-Xu recursion.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 10–12, Assumptions 2–5 and Theorems 3.2–3.3; pp. 12–14, Section 3.1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper assumes well-separated Z-roots, score smoothness, and minimum sampling probabilities; its Theorems 3.2–3.3 give deterministic Gaussian IPW-Z limits under scaled inverse-propensity convergence, while Section 3.1 presents a numerical clipped-LinUCB two-mode, non-Gaussian example.

Theorem 5.14 proves pointwise fixed-horizon realized-QV studentized asymptotic normality without deterministic variance stabilization; Design A has two post-burn-in propensity regimes and shows fixed-variance miscalibration.
The paper introduces directional stability as weaker than full-matrix stability and proves adaptive asymptotic normality and efficiency for scalar targets, including a LinUCB application.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 2 and 9, contribution statement and Theorem 1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper handles persistently adaptive M-estimation by consistently estimating time-varying score covariance matrices and then applying a variance-stabilized CLT; it does not use same-path realized-QV studentization.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 1–5, Abstract, equations (1.4)–(1.5), and Theorems 2.1/2.7 discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: For generalized Gaussian Thompson sampling, the paper proves non-degenerate random optimal-arm pull proportions described by an invariant SDE law and corresponding non-Gaussian normalized-arm-mean limits.

The article gives a lower bound on convergence to a prescribed point in its domain of attraction for stochastic-approximation recursions with finitely many possible limit points; it is not a global classification theorem for the specified recursion.

The work studies quantitative martingale CLT bounds through normalized predictable quadratic variation, including bounded-increment martingales; it does not supply adaptive-recursion attraction control.
